subject: environmental-science
title: Bottlenecks and Founder Effects
welcome_lead: Cheetahs, elephant seals, Pingelap blindness — populations that nearly disappeared.
meta_desc: A-Level Environmental Science adventure on bottlenecks, founder effects and gene flow.
final_note: Lost alleles do not return without gene flow — a bottleneck's shadow lasts thousands of generations.

concepts.def: Sharp reduction in population size, eroding allele diversity.
New population from a small founding group; non-random sample of alleles.
Movement of alleles between populations via migration.
Higher fitness of heterozygotes preserving diversity (e.g., sickle-cell).
Adding migrants to a small population to restore diversity (e.g., Florida panther).
Number of alleles at a locus; more sensitive than H to bottlenecks.

walkthroughs.body_html: African cheetahs show extreme genetic homogeneity, attributed to a Pleistocene bottleneck ~10 000 yr ago.
The Micronesian atoll's typhoon-survivor population (~20) carried an allele for colour blindness, now in ~10% of descendants.
Introducing 8 Texas pumas into the inbred Florida population restored heterozygosity and reversed fitness decline.

mcqs.q: Founder effects differ from bottlenecks because:

They involve selection only
They require mutation
They only occur in plants
Introducing new alleles via migrants
Removing deleterious alleles
Increasing census size only
Modifying the environment

options: They are alternative names for the same approach.
Services that ecosystems perform for themselves.

One is for plants, the other for animals.
Government services that protect nature.
Decomposition.
Services that ecosystems perform for themselves.
Benefits people obtain from ecosystems (pollination, water purification, climate regulation, food).
